questions.text_english: In case of association, abnormal molar mass of solute will
questions.solution: In association, solute molecules combine together to form larger aggregates, effectively reducing the number of particles in solution. Since molar mass is inversely proportional to the number of particles (via colligative properties), the observed (abnormal) molar mass increases. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because association always leads to a higher apparent molar mass, not a decrease or no change.

questions.text: Sn4+/Sn2+ युग्म के लिए मानक इलेक्ट्रोड विभव +0.15 V और Cr3+/Cr युग्म के लिए –0.74 V है। दो युग्म अपनी मानक अवस्थाओं में संयोजित होकर एक सेल का निर्माण करते हैं। सेल विभव होगा
questions.text_english: Standard electrode potential for Sn4+/Sn2+ couple is +0.15 V and that for the Cr3+/Cr couple is –0.74 V. The two couples in their standard states are connected to make a cell. The cell potential will be
questions.solution: Cell potential = E°cathode – E°anode. The Sn4+/Sn2+ couple has the higher (more positive) reduction potential (+0.15 V) so it acts as the cathode, and Cr3+/Cr (–0.74 V) acts as the anode. E°cell = +0.15 – (–0.74) = +0.15 + 0.74 = +0.89 V. Option B is correct. The other options arise from incorrect arithmetic or wrong assignment of cathode/anode.

questions.text: चुंबकीय आघूर्ण इसके प्रचक्रणी कोणीय संवेग और कक्षीय कोणीय संवेग से जुड़ा होता है। Cr3+ आयन (परमाणु क्रमांक : Cr = 24) का प्रचक्रण मात्र चुंबकीय आघूर्ण मान ________ है।
questions.text_english: The magnetic moment is associated with its spin angular momentum and orbital angular momentum. Spin only magnetic moment value of Cr3+ ion (Atomic no. : Cr = 24) is ________.
questions.solution: Cr has atomic number 24 with configuration [Ar] 3d5 4s1. Cr3+ loses 3 electrons giving configuration [Ar] 3d3, so there are 3 unpaired electrons (n = 3). Spin-only magnetic moment = √(n(n+2)) = √(3×5) = √15 ≈ 3.87 B.M. Hence option B is correct. Options A (2.87 B.M.) corresponds to n = 2, option C and D are not standard values for any whole number of unpaired electrons.

questions.text_english: Acidified KMnO4 oxidises sulphite to
questions.solution: Acidified KMnO4 is a strong oxidising agent. It oxidises sulphite ions (SO3²⁻, where S is in +4 oxidation state) to sulphate ions (SO4²⁻, where S is in +6 oxidation state). This is the complete oxidation product under acidic conditions. Options A, B, and C represent different or incomplete oxidation states of sulfur and are not the products of this particular reaction.

questions.text: [Pt(NH3)2Cl2]²+ का सही IUPAC नाम है
questions.text_english: The correct IUPAC name of [Pt(NH3)2Cl2]2+ is
questions.solution: In [Pt(NH3)2Cl2]2+, the two NH3 ligands are neutral (ammine) and the two Cl– ligands carry –1 charge each. Overall complex charge is 2+, so: Pt + 2(0) + 2(–1) = +2, giving Pt oxidation state = +2. The IUPAC name is Diamminedichloridoplatinum(II). Since the complex is cationic, the suffix '-um' (not '-ate') is used. Option B gives wrong oxidation state IV, option C gives 0, and option D uses '-ate' which is for anionic complexes.

questions.text_english: Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their boiling points: (i) (CH3)2CHCH2Br  (ii) CH3CH2CH2CH2Br  (iii) (CH3)3CBr
questions.image_description: Three structural formulae of butyl bromide isomers: (i) isobutyl bromide with CH3 groups on the central carbon, (ii) n-butyl bromide (straight chain), and (iii) tert-butyl bromide with three CH3 groups on the carbon bearing Br.
questions.solution: Boiling point of alkyl halides depends on the surface area available for van der Waals interactions. More branching reduces surface area and lowers boiling point. Compound (iii) is tert-butyl bromide (most branched, least surface area, lowest b.p.), compound (i) is isobutyl bromide (moderately branched), and compound (ii) is n-butyl bromide (straight chain, maximum surface area, highest b.p.). Therefore the correct increasing order is (iii) < (i) < (ii), which is option C.

questions.text_english: Alkyl halides undergoing nucleophilic bimolecular substitution reaction involve
questions.solution: In an SN2 (nucleophilic bimolecular substitution) reaction, the nucleophile attacks the carbon from the back side (opposite to the leaving group) in a single concerted step, leading to Walden inversion, i.e., complete inversion of configuration at the chiral centre. Retention of configuration (A) occurs in SN1 with neighbouring group participation; racemic mixture (B) is characteristic of SN1; formation of carbocation (D) is a feature of SN1. Hence option C is correct.

questions.text_english: Which is the correct order of acid strength from the following?
questions.solution: Phenol (C6H5OH) is the strongest acid among the three because the phenoxide ion formed after losing a proton is stabilised by resonance with the benzene ring. Water (H2O) is more acidic than aliphatic alcohols (ROH) because the alkyl group in alcohols donates electrons, increasing electron density on oxygen and making it harder to release a proton. Hence the correct order of acid strength is C6H5OH > H2O > ROH, which is option A.

questions.text_english: The acid formed when propyl magnesium bromide is treated with CO2 followed by acid hydrolysis is:
questions.solution: In the Grignard reaction with CO2, the Grignard reagent acts as a nucleophile and attacks the carbon of CO2 to form a magnesium salt of a carboxylic acid. When propyl magnesium bromide (C3H7MgBr) reacts with CO2, it gives C3H7COOMgBr as an intermediate, which on acid hydrolysis yields C3H7COOH (butanoic acid). Option A is correct. Option B would result from ethyl Grignard, option C from methyl Grignard, and option D is an alcohol, not a carboxylic acid.

questions.solution: To convert an amide (RCONH2) to an amine (RCH2NH2) with the same number of carbon atoms, reduction is required. LiAlH4 (lithium aluminium hydride) in ether is the best reagent for this purpose as it reduces the amide to a primary amine without changing the carbon chain length. questions.solution: Glucose exists predominantly in the pyranose (six-membered ring) form, not in the furanose (five-membered ring) form. Fructose is the sugar commonly found in the furanose form. Statements A (glucose is an aldohexose), B (glucose on heating with HI gives n-hexane confirming a straight 6-carbon chain), and D (glucose does not give Schiff's test in its cyclic form under normal conditions) are all true. Therefore, statement C is not true about glucose.

options.B: यह उत्क्रम परासरण के कारण जल खो देता है।

questions.solution: When an unripe mango is placed in a concentrated salt solution, the concentration of the solution outside the mango is higher than inside its cells. By osmosis, water moves from the region of lower solute concentration (inside the mango cells) to the region of higher solute concentration (the salt solution), causing the mango to lose water and shrivel. This is normal osmosis, not reverse osmosis. Option D is correct.

questions.solution: A homoleptic complex is one in which the central metal ion is coordinated to only one type of ligand. In both [Cr(H2O)6]Cl2 and [Fe(H2O)6]Cl2, the metal centre is surrounded exclusively by water (H2O) ligands in the coordination sphere, making them homoleptic complexes. The Cl– ions are outside the coordination sphere as counter ions. The Reason correctly explains why these are homoleptic — all ligands around the metal are the same (H2O). Hence both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A. Option A is correct.

Hence both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A. Option B is correct.

questions.text_english:
(A) Give reasons:
(a) Cooking is faster in pressure cooker than in an open pan.
(b) On mixing liquid X and liquid Y, volume of the resulting solution decreases. What type of deviation from Raoult's law is shown by the resulting solution? What change in temperature would you observe after mixing liquids X and Y?

OR

(B) Define Azeotrope. What type of Azeotrope is formed by negative deviation from Raoult's law? Give an example.

key_points: (a) In a pressure cooker, the pressure above the liquid is higher than atmospheric pressure, which raises the boiling point of water, so cooking occurs at a higher temperature and is therefore faster.
(b) Negative deviation from Raoult's law; temperature increases (exothermic mixing).

questions.solution:
(A)(a) In a pressure cooker, steam is not allowed to escape freely, which builds up pressure above the water. According to the relationship between boiling point and pressure, an increase in pressure raises the boiling point of water above 100°C. Consequently, food cooks at a higher temperature in a pressure cooker than in an open pan, making the process significantly faster.

(b) When the volume of a mixture is less than the sum of individual volumes of X and Y, it indicates that the intermolecular attractive forces between X and Y molecules are stronger than those between X-X or Y-Y molecules. This results in negative deviation from Raoult's law (observed vapour pressure is less than calculated). The stronger interactions release energy, so the temperature of the resulting solution increases (the mixing is exothermic).

(B) An azeotrope is a mixture of two or more liquids whose composition remains constant upon boiling, i.e., the mixture boils at a constant temperature and the vapour has the same composition as the liquid. When a solution shows negative deviation from Raoult's law, the intermolecular forces in the mixture are stronger, leading to a lower vapour pressure. Such solutions form maximum boiling azeotropes. Example: a mixture of HNO3 (68%) and water (32%) boils at 393.5 K.

questions.solution:
(a) In acidic medium, permanganate (MnO4⁻) acts as an oxidising agent. Mn goes from +7 to +2 (gain of 5e⁻ per Mn). Iodide (I⁻) is oxidised to I2 (each I loses 1e⁻, so 2I⁻ lose 2e⁻ to form I2). The balanced equation is:
2MnO4⁻(aq) + 10I⁻(aq) + 16H⁺(aq) → 2Mn²⁺(aq) + 5I2(s) + 8H2O(l)

(b) Dichromate (Cr2O7²⁻) oxidises Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺ in acidic medium. Each Cr goes from +6 to +3 (gain of 3e⁻); two Cr atoms gain 6e⁻ total. Six Fe²⁺ each lose 1e⁻ to become Fe³⁺, total 6e⁻ lost. The balanced equation is:
Cr2O7²⁻(aq) + 6Fe²⁺(aq) + 14H⁺(aq) → 2Cr³⁺(aq) + 6Fe³⁺(aq) + 7H2O(l)

questions.text: क्या आप अपेक्षा करते हैं कि प्रोपेनल की तुलना में बेंजैल्डिहाइड नाभिकरागी योगज अभिक्रियाओं में अधिक अभिक्रियाशील या कम अभिक्रियाशील होगा ? अपना उत्तर स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Would you expect benzaldehyde to be more reactive or less reactive in nucleophilic addition reactions than propanal? Justify your answer.

key_points: Benzaldehyde is less reactive than propanal in nucleophilic addition reactions.
The phenyl group delocalises the lone pair/electron density via resonance, reducing the partial positive charge on the carbonyl carbon.
The bulkier phenyl group also causes steric hindrance.

questions.solution: Benzaldehyde is less reactive than propanal in nucleophilic addition reactions. In benzaldehyde, the carbonyl carbon is attached to a phenyl group. The phenyl ring delocalises the electrons of the carbonyl group through resonance, which reduces the partial positive charge on the carbonyl carbon and makes it less susceptible to nucleophilic attack. Additionally, the bulky phenyl group causes steric hindrance, further reducing reactivity. In contrast, propanal has an ethyl group (–CH2CH3) attached to the carbonyl carbon; the alkyl group is electron-donating (+I effect), but it does not delocalize the charge through resonance, so propanal retains a higher electrophilic character at the carbonyl carbon and is more reactive toward nucleophiles.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित प्रत्येक अनुक्रम अभिक्रिया में A और B की पहचान कीजिए :
(a) CH3CH2Cl —(NaCN)→ A —(H2/Ni)→ B
(b) C6H5NH2 —(NaNO2/HCl, 0–5°C)→ A —(C6H5NH2/H+)→ B
questions.text_english:
Identify A and B in each of the following reaction sequence:
(a) CH3CH2Cl —(NaCN)→ A —(H2/Ni)→ B
(b) C6H5NH2 —(NaNO2/HCl, 0–5°C)→ A —(C6H5NH2/H+)→ B

key_points: (a) A = CH3CH2CN (propionitrile/propanenitrile); B = CH3CH2CH2NH2 (propan-1-amine)
(b) A = C6H5N2+Cl⁻ (benzene diazonium chloride); B = C6H5–NH–C6H5 (diphenylamine / N-phenylaniline)

questions.solution:
(a) CH3CH2Cl reacts with NaCN in an SN2 reaction; the cyanide ion (CN⁻) replaces Cl⁻ to give A = CH3CH2CN (propanenitrile). On catalytic hydrogenation with H2/Ni, the nitrile group (–CN) is reduced to –CH2NH2, giving B = CH3CH2CH2NH2 (propan-1-amine).

(b) C6H5NH2 (aniline) reacts with NaNO2 and HCl at 0–5°C (diazotisation) to give A = C6H5N2+Cl⁻ (benzene diazonium chloride). On coupling with C6H5NH2 (aniline) in the presence of H⁺, the diazonium salt undergoes a coupling reaction with aniline to give B = C6H5–NH–N=N–C6H5? Actually the product is diazoaminobenzene (C6H5–N=N–NH–C6H5) under weakly acidic/neutral conditions. Under H⁺ conditions as stated in the paper, the product is N-phenylaniline (diphenylamine, C6H5NHC6H5) via reduction, but the standard product of coupling of diazonium with aniline in acidic medium is p-aminoazobenzene (p-H2N–C6H4–N=N–C6H5). B = p-aminoazobenzene.

questions.text:
D-ग्लूकोज़ को निम्नलिखित अभिकर्मकों के साथ अभिक्रियित करने पर होने वाली अभिक्रियाएँ लिखिए :
(a) HCN
(b) Br2 जल
questions.text_english:
Write the reactions involved when D-glucose is treated with the following reagents:
(a) HCN
(b) Br2 water

key_points: (a) D-Glucose + HCN → D-Glucosecyanohydrin (addition of HCN to the aldehyde group giving a cyanohydrin with a new chiral centre, producing a mixture of epimers)
(b) D-Glucose + Br2 water → D-Gluconic acid (the aldehyde group –CHO is oxidised to –COOH)

questions.solution:
(a) D-Glucose contains a free aldehyde group (–CHO). When treated with HCN, nucleophilic addition takes place: the CN⁻ ion attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of glucose and H⁺ adds to the oxygen to give a cyanohydrin. The reaction is: D-Glucose (–CHO) + HCN → D-Glucose cyanohydrin (–CH(OH)–CN). A new chiral centre is created giving a mixture of two epimeric cyanohydrins (D-gluconic acid nitrile and D-mannonic acid nitrile on hydrolysis).

(b) Bromine water oxidises only the aldehyde group of glucose without affecting the ketone or other functional groups. The reaction is: D-Glucose (–CHO) + Br2 + H2O → D-Gluconic acid (–COOH) + 2HBr. Br2 water is selective and does not oxidise ketones (fructose does not react), so this reaction is used to distinguish aldoses from ketoses.

questions.text: जल में ग्लूकोस (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 180 g mol⁻¹) के विलयन का क्वथनांक 100.20 °C है। उसी विलयन के हिमांक की गणना करें। पानी के लिए, Kf और Kb मोलल स्थिरांक क्रमशः 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹ और 0.512 K kg mol⁻¹ हैं।
questions.text_english: A solution of glucose (molar mass = 180 g mol⁻¹) in water has a boiling point of 100.20 °C. Calculate the freezing point of the same solution. Molal constants for water Kf and Kb are 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹ and 0.512 K kg mol⁻¹ respectively.

key_points: Freezing point = 0 – 0.727 = –0.727 °C

questions.solution: The boiling point elevation is ΔTb = 100.20 – 100.00 = 0.20 K. Using the formula ΔTb = Kb × m, the molality of the solution is m = ΔTb / Kb = 0.20 / 0.512 = 0.3906 mol kg⁻¹. Since the same solution is used, its molality remains the same. The freezing point depression is ΔTf = Kf × m = 1.86 × 0.3906 = 0.727 K. The freezing point of water is 0°C, therefore the freezing point of the solution = 0 – 0.727 = –0.727 °C.
questions.topic: Colligative Properties – Elevation in Boiling Point and Depression in Freezing Point

questions.text:
(a) निम्न को समझाइए :
(i) आयनों के स्वतंत्र अभिगमन का कोलराऊश नियम
(ii) फैराडे के विद्युत-अपघटन का प्रथम नियम

(b) नीचे दिए गए E° मानों का उपयोग करते हुए, प्रागुक्ति कीजिए कि संक्षारण रोकने के लिए लोहे की सतह पर लेपन के लिए कौन–सा बेहतर है और क्यों।
दिया गया है : E°X²⁺/X = –2.36 V, E°Y²⁺/Y = –0.14 V, E°Fe²⁺/Fe = –0.44 V
questions.text_english:
(a) State the following:
(i) Kohlrausch law of independent migration of ions
(ii) Faraday's first law of electrolysis.

(b) Using E° values of X and Y given below, predict which is better for coating the surface of iron to prevent corrosion and why?
Given E°X²⁺/X = –2.36 V, E°Y²⁺/Y = –0.14 V, E°Fe²⁺/Fe = –0.44 V

key_points: Kohlrausch's law: the molar conductivity of an electrolyte at infinite dilution is the sum of the contributions of all its ions.
Faraday's first law: the mass of substance deposited/liberated at an electrode is directly proportional to the quantity of charge passed.
Metal X (E° = –2.36 V) is better because it is more active than iron and provides cathodic protection.

questions.solution:
(a)(i) Kohlrausch's Law of Independent Migration of Ions: The molar conductivity of an electrolyte at infinite dilution is equal to the sum of the molar ionic conductivities of the constituent cations and anions, each multiplied by their respective stoichiometric coefficients. Each ion migrates independently and contributes a fixed amount to the total molar conductivity, regardless of the nature of the co-ion. Mathematically, Λ°m = ν⁺λ°₊ + ν⁻λ°₋.

(ii) Faraday's First Law of Electrolysis: The mass of a substance deposited or liberated at an electrode during electrolysis is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity (charge) passed through the electrolyte. Mathematically, m = Z × Q = Z × I × t, where Z is the electrochemical equivalent of the substance.

(b) Metal X has E° = –2.36 V, which is much lower (more negative) than E° of Fe (–0.44 V). This means X is a more active metal than iron. When iron is coated with X, even if the coating is scratched, X acts as a sacrificial anode and gets oxidised preferentially, thereby protecting iron from corrosion. Metal Y (E° = –0.14 V) is less active (nobler) than iron; if the Y coating is damaged, the exposed iron would corrode faster. Therefore, metal X is the better choice for coating iron to prevent corrosion.
questions.topic: Kohlrausch's Law / Faraday's Laws / Corrosion Prevention

questions.text:
कोई अभिक्रिया 300 K पर 20 मिनट में 50% पूर्ण हो जाती है और वही अभिक्रिया 350 K पर 5 मिनट में 50% पूर्ण हो जाती है। यदि यह अभिक्रिया प्रथम कोटि की है तो सक्रियण ऊर्जा की गणना कीजिए।
[R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; log 4 = 0.602]
questions.text_english:
A certain reaction is 50% complete in 20 minutes at 300 K and the same reaction is 50% complete in 5 minutes at 350 K. Calculate the activation energy if it is a first order reaction.
[R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; log 4 = 0.602]

key_points: For first order: t½ is independent of concentration, so k ∝ 1/t½.

questions.solution: For a first order reaction, t½ = 0.693/k. The time for 50% completion is the half-life. At 300 K, t½ = 20 min, so k1 = 0.693/20 min⁻¹. At 350 K, t½ = 5 min, so k2 = 0.693/5 min⁻¹. Therefore k2/k1 = 20/5 = 4, and log(k2/k1) = log 4 = 0.602. Using the Arrhenius equation in the form: log(k2/k1) = Ea/(2.303R) × (T2–T1)/(T1×T2), we get 0.602 = Ea / (2.303 × 8.314) × (350–300)/(300×350). Solving: Ea = 0.602 × 2.303 × 8.314 × (300×350)/50 = 0.602 × 2.303 × 8.314 × 2100 = 0.602 × 19147.2 ≈ 41,820 J mol⁻¹ ≈ 41.8 kJ mol⁻¹. The activation energy for this reaction is approximately 41.8 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.text:
3d संक्रमण श्रेणी के तत्व इस प्रकार दिए गए हैं : Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn
निम्नलिखित का उत्तर दीजिए :
(a) कॉपर का E°M²⁺/M मान असाधारण रूप से धनात्मक है, क्यों ?
(b) कौन सा तत्व +2 ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था में एक प्रबल अपचायक है और क्यों ?
(c) Zn²⁺ लवण रंगहीन होते हैं, क्यों ?
questions.text_english:
The elements of 3d transition series are given as: Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn
Answer the following:
(a) Copper has exceptionally positive E°M²⁺/M value, why?
(b) Which element is a strong reducing agent in +2 oxidation state and why?
(c) Zn²⁺ salts are colourless. Why?

key_points: (a) Copper has high sublimation enthalpy and low hydration enthalpy, making its standard electrode potential exceptionally positive (+0.34 V).
(b) Mn in +2 state (Mn²⁺) or Ti³⁺ is a strong reducing agent due to electronic configuration stability.
(c) Zn²⁺ has a 3d¹⁰ configuration with no unpaired d-electrons, so no d-d transitions are possible and the salts are colourless.

questions.solution:
(a) Copper has an exceptionally positive standard electrode potential (E°Cu²⁺/Cu = +0.34 V) compared to other 3d metals. This is because copper has a very high enthalpy of atomisation (sublimation) due to strong metallic bonding from its partially filled d-orbitals, and relatively low hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺ ions. The energy required to convert Cu(s) to Cu²⁺(aq) is not sufficiently compensated by the hydration enthalpy, making copper resistant to oxidation and giving it a positive E° value.

(b) Titanium in +2 oxidation state (Ti²⁺ or Ti³⁺) is a strong reducing agent. However, Mn²⁺ is not particularly reducing. Among 3d series, Ti³⁺ is the strongest reducing agent in the lower oxidation state because it has a strong tendency to attain the more stable Ti⁴⁺ configuration. In the +2 state, Ti²⁺ with configuration [Ar]3d² readily loses electrons to reach Ti³⁺ or Ti⁴⁺, acting as a powerful reductant.

(c) Zn²⁺ salts are colourless because zinc in the +2 state has the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰. With all d-orbitals completely filled, there are no unpaired electrons and no empty d-orbitals available for d-d electronic transitions. Since the colour of transition metal ions arises from d-d transitions, the absence of such transitions in Zn²⁺ means it does not absorb visible light, making its compounds colourless.

questions.text_english:
(A) Draw the structure of the major monohalo product for each of the following reaction:
(a) 4-chloroethylbenzene + Br2, Heat →
(b) 1-methylcyclohexene + HBr →
(c) 4-(hydroxymethyl)phenol + HCl, Heat →

OR

(B) How do you convert:
(a) Chlorobenzene to biphenyl
(b) Propene to 1-Iodopropane
(c) 2-bromobutane to but-2-ene

key_points: (A)(a) Br substitutes on the benzylic –CH2– carbon (radical halogenation at the benzylic position): 4-Cl-C6H4-CHBr-CH3
(A)(b) Markovnikov addition: Br adds to the more substituted carbon (C1): 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane
(A)(c) –OH groups (both phenolic and benzylic) react with HCl; phenolic OH is less reactive; the benzylic CH2OH reacts to give CH2Cl product: 4-hydroxybenzyl chloride
(B)(a) Chlorobenzene + Na/dry ether (Wurtz-Fittig) or Cu/300°C (Ullmann reaction) → Biphenyl
(B)(b) Propene + HI (anti-Markovnikov via peroxide/radical) → 1-Iodopropane (using HBr/peroxide then NaI/acetone) OR propene + HBr/peroxide → 1-bromopropane, then NaI → 1-iodopropane
(B)(c) 2-bromobutane + alcoholic KOH (E2 elimination) → But-2-ene

questions.solution:
(A)(a) The reaction of 4-chloroethylbenzene with Br2 in the presence of heat proceeds via free radical mechanism. Halogenation occurs preferentially at the benzylic position (–CH2–) because the benzylic radical is stabilised by resonance with the aromatic ring. The major product is 4-ClC6H4–CHBr–CH3 (1-bromo-1-(4-chlorophenyl)ethane).

(A)(b) Addition of HBr to 1-methylcyclohexene follows Markovnikov's rule. H⁺ adds to the carbon bearing fewer alkyl substituents (C2, the =CH–), and Br⁻ adds to the more substituted carbon (C1, the =C(CH3)–). The major product is 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane.

(A)(c) 4-(Hydroxymethyl)phenol has both a phenolic –OH and a benzylic –CH2OH group. With HCl and heat, the benzylic –CH2OH undergoes substitution more readily (SN1 via benzylic carbocation) than the phenolic –OH. The major product is 4-hydroxybenzyl chloride (4-HO-C6H4-CH2Cl).

(B)(a) Chlorobenzene → Biphenyl: The Ullmann reaction is used. Two moles of chlorobenzene are coupled in the presence of copper powder at 300°C: 2 C6H5Cl + Cu → C6H5–C6H5 + CuCl2.

(B)(b) Propene → 1-Iodopropane: First, propene reacts with HBr in the presence of peroxides (anti-Markovnikov/radical addition) to give 1-bromopropane. Then, 1-bromopropane is treated with NaI in acetone (Finkelstein reaction) to give 1-iodopropane: CH3CH2CH2Br + NaI → CH3CH2CH2I + NaBr.

(B)(c) 2-Bromobutane → But-2-ene: Treat 2-bromobutane with alcoholic KOH (strong base, E2 elimination). The base abstracts a beta-hydrogen and Br⁻ leaves simultaneously to give the more substituted alkene. The major product is but-2-ene (CH3–CH=CH–CH3).

(a) निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को उनके क्वथनांक के बढ़ते क्रम में व्यवस्थित करें :

(b) निम्नलिखित में से प्रत्येक के लिए संभावित स्पष्टीकरण दीजिए :
(i) ऐरोमैटिक प्राथमिक ऐमीनों को गैब्रिएल थैलामाइड संश्लेषण से नहीं बनाया जा सकता।
(ii) एमाइड, ऐमीनों की तुलना में कम क्षारकीय होते हैं।
questions.text_english:
(a) Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their boiling point:
(CH3)2NH, CH3CH2NH2, CH3CH2OH.

(b) Give plausible explanation for each of the following:
(i) Aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by Gabriel Phthalimide synthesis.
(ii) Amides are less basic than amines.

key_points: (a) (CH3)2NH < CH3CH2NH2 < CH3CH2OH
(b)(i) Gabriel synthesis requires N-alkylation of phthalimide using alkyl halides (SN2), but aryl halides do not undergo SN2 reactions.
(b)(ii) In amides, the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalised into the C=O group via resonance, reducing its availability for protonation.

questions.solution:
(a) Among the three compounds, ethanol (CH3CH2OH) has the highest boiling point because it forms strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds (O–H···O). Between the two amines, ethylamine (CH3CH2NH2) is a primary amine with two N–H bonds and forms stronger hydrogen bonds than dimethylamine ((CH3)2NH) which is a secondary amine with only one N–H bond and a bulkier structure offering less effective hydrogen bonding. Therefore the increasing order of boiling points is: (CH3)2NH < CH3CH2NH2 < CH3CH2OH.

(b)(i) Gabriel phthalimide synthesis involves the alkylation of the phthalimide anion with an alkyl halide via SN2 mechanism. Aryl halides (like C6H5–X) do not undergo SN2 reactions because the phenyl carbon bearing the halogen is sp² hybridised, and the benzene ring creates too much steric hindrance for backside attack. Hence aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by this route.

(b)(ii) In amines, the lone pair on nitrogen is readily available to accept a proton, making them basic. In amides (RCONH2), the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalised by resonance with the adjacent carbonyl (C=O) group: –NH2 donates electrons to C=O, forming a partial double bond (–NH=C–O⁻). This resonance significantly reduces the electron density on nitrogen, making the lone pair far less available for protonation. Hence amides are much weaker bases than amines.
questions.topic: Boiling Points of Amines / Gabriel Synthesis / Basicity of Amides

(b) निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा एक डाइसैकैराइड है ? ग्लूकोज़, लैक्टोज़, ऐमिलोज़, फ्रक्टोज़

questions.text_english:
(a) What is the difference between native protein and denatured protein?
(b) Which one of the following is a disaccharide? Glucose, Lactose, Amylose, Fructose
(c) Which vitamin is responsible for the coagulation of blood?

key_points: (a) Native protein has its natural three-dimensional structure maintained by hydrogen bonds, disulfide bridges, and hydrophobic interactions; denatured protein has lost this structure due to heat, acid, or other agents.
(b) Lactose is a disaccharide.
(c) Vitamin K is responsible for blood coagulation.

questions.solution:
(a) A native protein is one that has its complete, naturally occurring three-dimensional structure (primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary structures) intact. This structure is maintained by various non-covalent interactions such as hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, van der Waals forces, and covalent disulfide bridges. A denatured protein is one that has lost its higher-order three-dimensional structure due to the disruption of these interactions by physical agents (heat, UV radiation) or chemical agents (acids, bases, detergents). Denaturation does not break the peptide bonds, so the primary structure (amino acid sequence) remains intact, but biological activity is usually lost.

(b) Lactose is a disaccharide. It is formed by the condensation of one molecule of glucose and one molecule of galactose joined by a glycosidic bond. Glucose and fructose are monosaccharides, while amylose is a polysaccharide (a component of starch).

(c) Vitamin K is responsible for the coagulation (clotting) of blood. It acts as a cofactor for the synthesis of prothrombin and several other clotting factors in the liver. Deficiency of Vitamin K leads to impaired blood clotting.

questions.text: रासायनिक अभिक्रिया का वेग या तो प्रति इकाई समय में अभिकारक की सांद्रता में कमी या उत्पाद की सांद्रता में वृद्धि के रूप में व्यक्त किया जाता है। अभिक्रिया का वेग अभिकारकों की प्रकृति, अभिकारकों की सांद्रता, तापमान, उत्प्रेरक की उपस्थिति, अभिकारकों के पृष्ठीय क्षेत्रफल और प्रकाश की उपस्थिति पर निर्भर करता है। अभिक्रिया का वेग अभिकारक की सांद्रता से सीधे संबंधित होता है। वेग नियम बताता है कि अभिक्रिया का वेग सांद्रता पदों पर निर्भर करता है जिस पर अभिक्रिया का वेग वास्तव में निर्भर करता है, जैसा कि प्रयोगात्मक रूप से देखा गया है। वेग नियम अभिव्यक्ति में अभिकारकों की सांद्रता की घातों के योग को अभिक्रिया की कोटि कहा जाता है जबकि एक प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया में भाग लेने वाली स्पीशीज़ की संख्या जो रासायनिक अभिक्रिया सम्पन्न करने के लिए एक साथ संघट्ट करती है, अभिक्रिया की आण्विकता कहलाती है।
questions.text_english: The rate of a chemical reaction is expressed either in terms of decrease in the concentration of reactants or increase in the concentration of a product per unit time. Rate of the reaction depends upon the nature of reactants, concentration of reactants, temperature, presence of catalyst, surface area of the reactants and presence of light. Rate of reaction is directly related to the concentration of reactant. Rate law states that the rate of reaction depends upon the concentration terms on which the rate of reaction actually depends, as observed experimentally. The sum of powers of the concentration of the reactants in the Rate law expression is called order of reaction while the number of reacting species taking part in an elementary reaction which must collide simultaneously in order to bring about a chemical reaction is called molecularity of the reaction.

questions.topic: Rate of Reaction, Order and Molecularity

sub_questions.text_english: What is a rate determining step?

key_points: The slowest step in a multi-step reaction mechanism that determines the overall rate of the reaction.

sub_questions.solution: The rate determining step is the slowest step in a complex (multi-step) reaction mechanism. Since all intermediate steps must occur for the reaction to be completed, the overall rate of the reaction cannot be faster than the slowest step. It acts like the bottleneck that controls the rate of the entire reaction.

key_points: A complex reaction is one that proceeds through more than one elementary step, involving one or more reaction intermediates.

sub_questions.solution: A complex reaction is a reaction that does not occur in a single step but proceeds through a series of elementary steps. It involves the formation of one or more intermediate species that are not present in the overall balanced equation. The overall rate of the complex reaction is governed by the slowest elementary step, called the rate-determining step.

sub_questions.text: वेग स्थिरांक पर ताप का क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What is the effect of temperature on the rate constant of a reaction?

key_points: The rate constant increases with increase in temperature. As a general rule, the rate constant roughly doubles for every 10°C rise in temperature (Arrhenius equation: k = Ae^(-Ea/RT)).

sub_questions.solution: The rate constant (k) of a reaction increases with an increase in temperature. According to the Arrhenius equation, k = Ae^(–Ea/RT), as temperature T increases, the exponential term increases, resulting in a larger value of k. As a general approximation, the rate constant approximately doubles for every 10 K (or 10°C) rise in temperature.

sub_questions.text: आण्विकता केवल प्राथमिक अभिक्रियाओं के लिए ही क्यों लागू होती है जबकि कोटि प्राथमिक और जटिल अभिक्रिया दोनों के लिए लागू होती हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is molecularity applicable only for elementary reactions whereas order is applicable for elementary as well as complex reactions?

key_points: Molecularity is a theoretical concept defined for a single step; for complex reactions, each step has its own molecularity but the overall reaction does not have a meaningful single molecularity. Order is determined experimentally from the rate law and applies to any reaction.

sub_questions.solution: Molecularity is defined as the number of reacting molecules/species that collide simultaneously in a single elementary step to bring about a chemical reaction. For a complex (multi-step) reaction, each individual elementary step has its own molecularity, but the overall reaction cannot be assigned a single molecularity because it does not occur in one step. Order, on the other hand, is an experimentally determined quantity from the rate law expression (r = k[A]^m[B]^n) and can be applied to both elementary and complex reactions. For complex reactions, the order reflects the rate-determining step.

sub_questions.text: अणु X का Y में रूपांतरण द्वितीय कोटि की बलगतिकी के अनुरूप होता है। यदि X की सांद्रता तीन गुनी कर दी जाए तो Y के निर्माण होने के वेग पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ेगा ?
sub_questions.text_english: The conversion of molecule X to Y follows second order kinetics. If concentration of X is increased 3 times, how will it affect the rate of formation of Y?

key_points: The rate will increase 9 times (3² = 9).

sub_questions.solution: For a second order reaction, the rate law is: Rate = k[X]². If the concentration of X is increased 3 times (i.e., [X] becomes 3[X]), then new rate = k(3[X])² = 9k[X]² = 9 × original rate. Therefore, the rate of formation of Y will increase 9 times.

questions.text: बेन्जीन वलय से जुड़े OH समूह के प्रबल सक्रियण प्रभाव के कारण फीनॉल आसानी से इलेक्ट्रॉनरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रियाएँ देते हैं। चूँकि OH समूह o– और p– स्थितियों पर इलेक्ट्रॉन घनत्व को अधिक बढ़ाता है, इसलिए OH समूह ऑर्थो और पैरा निर्देशक होता है। राइमर–टीमन इलेक्ट्रॉनरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया के उदाहरण में से एक है। जिसके द्वारा फीनॉल की ऐरोमैटिक वलय में हाइड्रॉक्सिल समूह की ऑर्थो स्थिति पर एल्डिहाइड समूह प्रवेश कर जाता है। यह एक सामान्य विधि है जो फीनॉलों के ऑर्थो फॉर्मिलन के लिए प्रयुक्त की जाती है।
questions.text_english: Phenols undergo electrophilic substitution reactions readily due to the strong activating effect of OH group attached to the benzene ring. Since, the OH group increases the electron density more to o– and p– positions therefore OH group is ortho, para-directing. Reimer-Tiemann reaction is one of the examples of aldehyde group being introduced on the aromatic ring of phenol, ortho to the hydroxyl group. This is a general method used for the ortho-formylation of phenols.

sub_questions.text:
क्या होता है जब फीनॉल निम्न से अभिक्रिया करता है ?
(i) Br2/CS2
(ii) सांद्र HNO3
sub_questions.text_english:
What happens when phenol reacts with:
(i) Br2/CS2
(ii) Conc. HNO3

key_points: (i) Phenol + Br2/CS2 → 2,4,6-tribromophenol (white precipitate) — actually in non-polar solvent (CS2), mono-bromination gives o- and p-bromophenol mixture.
(ii) Phenol + conc. HNO3 → 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid)

sub_questions.solution:
(i) When phenol reacts with Br2 in a non-polar solvent like CS2 (carbon disulfide), the reaction is controlled and gives a mixture of ortho-bromophenol and para-bromophenol (monobromination) because the electron density is highest at ortho and para positions due to the –OH group. If aqueous bromine water is used, white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol is formed immediately.

(ii) When phenol reacts with concentrated HNO3 (concentrated), vigorous nitration occurs at ortho and para positions. All three available positions (2, 4 and 6) undergo nitration to give 2,4,6-trinitrophenol, also known as picric acid, which is a yellow crystalline solid.

sub_questions.text: फीनॉल का प्रोटॉनन आसानी से क्यों नहीं होता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why phenol does not undergo protonation readily?

key_points: The lone pair on oxygen of phenol is delocalised into the benzene ring by resonance, reducing its availability for protonation.

sub_questions.solution: Phenol does not undergo protonation readily because the lone pair on the oxygen atom is involved in resonance with the benzene ring (p–π conjugation). This electron delocalisation reduces the electron density on oxygen, making it a poorer proton acceptor (weaker base) compared to aliphatic alcohols where the lone pair on oxygen is more available. The resonance stabilisation of phenol means its lone pair is less accessible for accepting a proton from an acid.

राइमर–टीमन अभिक्रिया में बनने वाले उत्पाद का IUPAC नाम लिखें।
sub_questions.text_english:
Which is a stronger acid – phenol or cresol? Give reason.

OR

Write the IUPAC name of the product formed in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction.

key_points: Phenol is a stronger acid than cresol because the methyl group in cresol is electron-donating (+I effect), increasing electron density on oxygen and making it harder to release a proton.
OR: IUPAC name of Reimer-Tiemann product = 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde)

sub_questions.solution:
Phenol is a stronger acid than cresol. Cresol is a methylphenol (methyl group attached to the benzene ring of phenol). The methyl group exerts an electron-donating inductive effect (+I effect), which increases the electron density on the oxygen atom. This makes it more difficult for cresol to release a proton (H⁺) compared to phenol. Therefore, the phenoxide ion is more stable (better resonance stabilisation without the electron-donating methyl group) than the cresolate ion, making phenol the stronger acid.

OR: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol reacts with chloroform (CHCl3) in the presence of aqueous NaOH (alkali). The electrophilic dichlorocarbene (:CCl2) attacks the ortho position of the phenol ring, and subsequent hydrolysis gives the aldehyde group. The product is 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde. Its IUPAC name is 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde.

questions.text:
(A)
(a) निम्नलिखित के लिए सेल अभिक्रिया लिखिए तथा 298 K पर सेल का e.m.f. परिकलित कीजिए :
Sn(s) | Sn²⁺ (0.004 M) || H⁺ (0.02 M) | H2(g) (1 Bar) | Pt(s)
(दिया गया है : E°Sn²⁺/Sn = –0.14 V, E°H⁺|H2(g),Pt = 0.00 V)

(b) निम्नलिखित के कारण बताइए :
(i) E° मानों के आधार पर, O2 गैस एनोड पर मुक्त होनी चाहिए, लेकिन जलीय NaCl के विद्युत अपघटन में Cl2 गैस मुक्त होती है।
(ii) तनुकरण पर CH3COOH की चालकता कम हो जाती है।
questions.text_english:
(A)
(a) Write the cell reaction and calculate the e.m.f. of the following cell at 298 K:
Sn(s) | Sn²⁺ (0.004 M) || H⁺ (0.02 M) | H2(g) (1 Bar) | Pt(s)
(Given : E°Sn²⁺/Sn = –0.14 V, E°H+|H2(g),Pt = 0.00 V)

(b) Account for the following:
(i) On the basis of E° values, O2 gas should be liberated at anode but it is Cl2 gas which is liberated in the electrolysis of aqueous NaCl.
(ii) Conductivity of CH3COOH decreases on dilution.

OR

(B)
(a) Write the anode and cathode reactions and the overall cell reaction occurring in a lead storage battery during its use.
(b) Calculate the potential for half-cell containing 0.01 M K2Cr2O7(aq), 0.01 M Cr³⁺(aq) and 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ M H⁺(aq). The half cell reaction is Cr2O7²⁻(aq) + 14H⁺(aq) + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺(aq) + 7H2O(l) and the standard electrode potential E° = 1.33 V. [Given: log 10 = 1]

key_points: (A)(a) Cell reaction: Sn(s) + 2H⁺(aq) → Sn²⁺(aq) + H2(g); E°cell = 0.00 – (–0.14) = +0.14 V; Apply Nernst equation to get Ecell.
(A)(b)(i) Overpotential: higher overpotential needed for O2 evolution than Cl2 at higher concentrations; Cl2 is preferentially liberated.
(A)(b)(ii) Conductivity (κ) decreases on dilution because the number of ions per unit volume decreases.
(B)(a) Anode: Pb → PbSO4; Cathode: PbO2 → PbSO4; Overall: Pb + PbO2 + 2H2SO4 → 2PbSO4 + 2H2O.
(B)(b) Apply Nernst equation to calculate E.

questions.solution:
(A)(a) Cell reaction: At the anode (oxidation): Sn(s) → Sn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻. At the cathode (reduction): 2H⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → H2(g). Overall cell reaction: Sn(s) + 2H⁺(aq) → Sn²⁺(aq) + H2(g). E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = 0.00 – (–0.14) = +0.14 V. Applying the Nernst equation at 298 K: Ecell = E°cell – (0.0591/n) × log([Sn²⁺]/[H⁺]²) = 0.14 – (0.0591/2) × log(0.004/(0.02)²) = 0.14 – (0.02955) × log(0.004/0.0004) = 0.14 – 0.02955 × log(10) = 0.14 – 0.02955 × 1 = 0.14 – 0.02955 ≈ 0.1105 V ≈ 0.11 V.

(A)(b)(i) Based on standard electrode potential values, the E° for O2/H2O (+1.23 V) is lower than E° for Cl2/Cl⁻ (+1.36 V), suggesting O2 should be liberated preferentially. However, in practice, the liberation of O2 requires a significantly higher overpotential (extra energy beyond thermodynamic requirement). At a sufficiently high concentration of Cl⁻ ions in aqueous NaCl, the effective potential required for Cl2 evolution becomes lower than that for O2, so Cl2 is evolved preferentially at the anode.

(A)(b)(ii) Conductivity (κ) of a solution is defined as the conductance per unit volume and depends on the number of ions per unit volume. CH3COOH is a weak acid and exists mostly as undissociated molecules. On dilution, the degree of dissociation increases (more CH3COOH dissociates into CH3COO⁻ and H⁺), but the total number of ions per unit volume decreases because the volume increases much more than the increase in dissociation. Since conductivity depends on the concentration of ions per cm³, it decreases on dilution despite the increase in molar conductivity.

(B)(a) Lead storage battery: During use (discharge), Anode (oxidation): Pb(s) + SO4²⁻(aq) → PbSO4(s) + 2e⁻. Cathode (reduction): PbO2(s) + SO4²⁻(aq) + 4H⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l). Overall cell reaction: Pb(s) + PbO2(s) + 2H2SO4(aq) → 2PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l).

(B)(b) The Nernst equation for the half-cell Cr2O7²⁻(aq) + 14H⁺(aq) + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺(aq) + 7H2O(l) is: E = E° – (0.0591/6) × log([Cr³⁺]²/([Cr2O7²⁻][H⁺]¹⁴]). Given: [K2Cr2O7] = 0.01 M so [Cr2O7²⁻] = 0.01 M; [Cr³⁺] = 0.01 M; [H⁺] = 1.0×10⁻⁴ M; E° = 1.33 V. Calculation: Q = (0.01)²/((0.01)(1×10⁻⁴)¹⁴) = (10⁻⁴)/((10⁻²)(10⁻⁵⁶)) = 10⁻⁴/(10⁻⁵⁸) = 10⁵⁴. log Q = 54. E = 1.33 – (0.0591/6) × 54 = 1.33 – (0.009850 × 54) = 1.33 – 0.5319 ≈ 0.798 V ≈ 0.80 V.

questions.text_english:
(A) Answer the following:
(a) Low spin tetrahedral complexes are not known.
(b) Co²⁺ is easily oxidised to Co³⁺ in the presence of a strong ligand. [At. No. of Co = 27]
(c) What type of isomerism is shown by the complex [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6]?
(d) Why a solution of [Ni(H2O)6]²⁺ is green while a solution of [Ni(CN)4]²⁻ is colourless. (At. No. of Ni = 28)
(e) Write the IUPAC name of the following complex: [Co(NH3)5(CO3)]Cl

OR

(B)
(a) What is meant by 'Chelate effect'? Give an example.
(b) Write the hybridization and magnetic behaviour of [Fe(CN)6]⁴⁻. (Atomic number: Fe = 26)
(c) If PtCl2 · 2NH3 does not react with AgNO3, what will be its formula?

key_points: (A)(a) In tetrahedral geometry, Δt (crystal field splitting) is much smaller (~4/9 Δo), insufficient to pair electrons; low spin state cannot be achieved.
(A)(b) In the presence of strong ligands, Co³⁺ (d⁶, low spin) forms very stable octahedral complexes with CFSE; Co²⁺ is easily oxidised to attain this stability.
(A)(c) Ionisation isomerism (the two ions can exchange ligands between coordination spheres).
(A)(d) [Ni(H2O)6]²⁺ has unpaired d-electrons allowing d-d transitions; [Ni(CN)4]²⁻ is square planar, low spin, d⁸ with all electrons paired, no d-d transitions.
(A)(e) Pentaamminecarbonato-O-cobalt(III) chloride.
(B)(a) Chelate effect: formation of chelate rings by polydentate ligands increases stability; e.g., [Cu(en)2]²⁺.
(B)(b) [Fe(CN)6]⁴⁻: Fe²⁺ is d⁶; CN⁻ strong field causes pairing; hybridisation d²sp³; diamagnetic.
(B)(c) [Pt(NH3)2Cl2] — it is the neutral complex with no ionisable Cl⁻.

questions.solution:
(A)(a) Low spin tetrahedral complexes are not known because the crystal field splitting energy in tetrahedral complexes (Δt) is only about 4/9 of that in octahedral complexes (Δo) for the same metal and ligands. This smaller Δt is generally less than the pairing energy (P) of electrons, meaning it is energetically more favourable for electrons to occupy higher energy orbitals with parallel spins rather than pair up. As a result, tetrahedral complexes are always high spin.

(A)(b) Co has atomic number 27, configuration [Ar] 3d⁷ 4s². Co²⁺ has configuration 3d⁷ (3 unpaired electrons, high spin in weak field). Co³⁺ has configuration 3d⁶. In the presence of a strong field ligand (like CN⁻ or NH3), the 3d⁶ configuration of Co³⁺ results in a very stable low-spin octahedral complex with large crystal field stabilisation energy (CFSE). This extra stability makes the Co³⁺ state energetically favoured, so Co²⁺ is readily oxidised to Co³⁺ in the presence of strong ligands.

(A)(c) The complex [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] shows coordination isomerism (also called ionisation isomerism in some texts). In this complex, the Co centre is surrounded by NH3 ligands and Cr by CN⁻ ligands. Its coordination isomer would be [Cr(NH3)6][Co(CN)6], where the ligands are exchanged between the two metal centres. This is coordination isomerism.

(A)(d) Ni has atomic number 28, configuration [Ar] 3d⁸ 4s². Ni²⁺ has configuration 3d⁸. In [Ni(H2O)6]²⁺, H2O is a weak field ligand; the complex is octahedral and high spin with 2 unpaired d-electrons. These unpaired electrons allow d-d electronic transitions that absorb specific wavelengths of visible light, giving the complex a green colour. In [Ni(CN)4]²⁻, CN⁻ is a very strong field ligand; the complex is square planar and low spin. In the square planar arrangement of Ni²⁺ (d⁸) with CN⁻, all electrons are paired (no unpaired electrons), so no d-d transitions can occur in the visible region, making the solution colourless.

(A)(e) In [Co(NH3)5(CO3)]Cl: the coordination sphere contains 5 ammine (NH3) ligands and one carbonate (CO3²⁻) ligand. Cl⁻ is the counter ion. Cobalt oxidation state: Co + 5(0) + (–2) = +1? Charge of complex cation = +1 (one Cl⁻ outside). So Co is +3. CO3²⁻ acts as monodentate (carbonato-O). IUPAC name: Carbonato-O-pentaamminecobalt(III) chloride.

(B)(a) Chelate effect refers to the enhanced stability of a complex formed by a polydentate (chelating) ligand compared to a complex with an equivalent number of monodentate ligands. Chelating ligands form ring structures (chelate rings) with the metal, and the resulting complex is more thermodynamically stable due to a favourable entropy contribution (one polydentate ligand replaces many monodentate ligands, releasing more solvent molecules and increasing entropy). Example: [Cu(en)2]²⁺ (where en = ethylenediamine, a bidentate ligand) is much more stable than [Cu(CH3NH2)4]²⁺.

(B)(b) Fe has atomic number 26, configuration [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s². In [Fe(CN)6]⁴⁻, Fe is in +2 state with 3d⁶ configuration. CN⁻ is a very strong field ligand, so it causes complete pairing of the 3d electrons. The 3d⁶ electrons pair up in three d-orbitals, leaving two empty d-orbitals. This allows d²sp³ hybridisation (two 3d, one 4s, three 4p orbitals) forming an inner orbital octahedral complex. Since all 6 d-electrons are paired, [Fe(CN)6]⁴⁻ is diamagnetic (no unpaired electrons).

(B)(c) PtCl2·2NH3 does not react with AgNO3, which means there are no free Cl⁻ ions outside the coordination sphere (no ionisable chloride). All chloride ions are inside the coordination sphere, bonded to Pt. The formula of the compound is therefore [Pt(NH3)2Cl2], i.e., diamminedichloridoplatinum(II), a neutral square planar complex.

(A)
(a) Carry out the following conversions:
(i) Ethanal to But-2-enal
(ii) Propanoic acid to ethane

(b) An alkene A with molecular formula C5H10 on ozonolysis gives a mixture of two compounds B and C. Compound B gives positive Fehling test and also reacts with iodine and NaOH solution. Compound C does not give Fehling solution test but forms iodoform. Identify the compounds A, B and C.

OR

(B) An organic compound (A) (molecular formula C8H16O2) was hydrolysed with dilute sulphuric acid to get a carboxylic acid (B) and an alcohol (C). Oxidation of (C) with chromic acid produced (B). (C) on dehydration gives But-1-ene. Identify (A), (B) and (C) and write chemical equations for the reactions involved.

key_points: (A)(a)(i) Ethanal → But-2-enal via Aldol condensation (two molecules of ethanal react in dilute NaOH to give aldol, then dehydration gives but-2-enal).
(A)(a)(ii) Propanoic acid → ethane via reduction of –COOH to –CH3 (decarboxylation with soda lime: CH3CH2COOH + NaOH/CaO → CH3CH3 + Na2CO3).

(A)(b) B gives Fehling test (aldehyde) and iodoform test (methyl ketone/CH3CHO) → B = CH3CHO (ethanal). C does not give Fehling but gives iodoform → C = CH3COCH3 (propanone). A = CH3CH=C(CH3)2 (2-methylbut-2-ene)... Reconsidering: A gives B+C on ozonolysis. B = CH3CHO, C = CH3COCH3. Atoms: B(C2H4O) + C(C3H6O) = C5H10O2; the alkene A = C5H10, consistent. A = 2-methylbut-2-ene: CH3–C(CH3)=CH–CH3; ozonolysis → CH3COCH3 (C) + CH3CHO (B). Correct.

(B) A = C8H16O2 (ester), hydrolysis gives B (carboxylic acid) and C (alcohol); oxidation of C gives B; C dehydrates to but-1-ene → C = butan-1-ol (C4H9OH); B = butanoic acid (C4H8O2). A = butyl butanoate (C4H9COOC4H9)... checking formula: C4H7O–O–C4H9 = C8H16O2. Yes! A = butyl butanoate.

questions.solution:
(A)(a)(i) Ethanal to But-2-enal: This conversion is achieved by an Aldol condensation reaction. Two molecules of ethanal (CH3CHO) react in the presence of dilute NaOH (aldol condensation) to form 3-hydroxybutanal (aldol product). On heating (dehydration), water is eliminated to give but-2-enal (CH3–CH=CH–CHO). Step 1 (Aldol addition): 2CH3CHO → CH3CH(OH)CH2CHO (dilute NaOH). Step 2 (Dehydration): CH3CH(OH)CH2CHO → CH3CH=CHCHO + H2O (heat).

(A)(a)(ii) Propanoic acid to Ethane: This is achieved by decarboxylation. Propanoic acid (CH3CH2COOH) is heated with soda lime (NaOH + CaO): CH3CH2COONa + NaOH → CH3CH3 + Na2CO3. The sodium salt of propanoic acid reacts with NaOH/CaO to lose CO2 (decarboxylation), giving ethane (CH3CH3).

(A)(b) Compound B gives positive Fehling test indicating it is an aldehyde. B also reacts with I2/NaOH (iodoform test) indicating presence of –CH3CO– or CH3CH(OH)– group. Since B is an aldehyde giving iodoform, B = CH3CHO (ethanal/acetaldehyde). Compound C does not give Fehling test (not an aldehyde) but gives iodoform, so C contains a CH3CO– group. C is a ketone: C = CH3COCH3 (propanone/acetone). Both B and C come from ozonolysis of alkene A (C5H10). Combining B (C2) + C (C3) = C5, consistent with C5H10. A is the alkene that on ozonolysis gives ethanal and acetone: A = 2-methylbut-2-ene (CH3–C(CH3)=CH–CH3). Ozonolysis: CH3–C(CH3)=CH–CH3 → CH3COCH3 (propanone, C) + CH3CHO (ethanal, B).

(B) Compound A has molecular formula C8H16O2 and is an ester (hydrolysis gives acid + alcohol). Alcohol C on dehydration gives but-1-ene (CH2=CH–CH2–CH3), which means C is butan-1-ol (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH = C4H9OH) since dehydration of a primary alcohol gives the terminal alkene. Oxidation of C (butan-1-ol) with chromic acid gives B: CH3CH2CH2CH2OH → CH3CH2CH2COOH (butanoic acid). So B = butanoic acid (C4H8O2). A is the ester of B and C: A = butyl butanoate, CH3CH2CH2COO–CH2CH2CH2CH3 (C8H16O2). 

Reactions:
1. Hydrolysis: CH3CH2CH2COOC4H9 + H2O → CH3CH2CH2COOH (B) + C4H9OH (C) [H2SO4, dilute]
2. Oxidation: C4H9OH + [O] (CrO3/H2SO4) → C4H8O2 (B) = CH3CH2CH2COOH
3. Dehydration: C4H9OH (butan-1-ol) → CH2=CHCH2CH3 (but-1-ene) + H2O [Al2O3/heat]
